Laura / team — quick preliminary technical notes from the runtime side: 

What I pulled (08:30–09:30 PT):
- Autoscaler events: several rapid scale-up/scale-down cycles targeting the yolk-13b-quantized pool starting at 08:28 (span ~6m). We saw instance churn ~3x the normal rate.
- Kernel-selection failures: transient kernel OOMs surfaced and retried; retries caused request queuing growth.
- KV cache invalidation: a subset of shards showed higher miss rates and increased cold-start latency for long context (seq_len > 1,024).
- No model variant rollouts recorded in the control plane during that window.

Immediate mitigations performed (09:10 PT):
- Pinned yolk-13b traffic to the stable quantized runtime (fallback) to avoid kernel OOM retry path.
- Disabled aggressive scale-down policy for the affected pool to prevent thrash.

Result: error-rate dropped from 4.3% → 1.1% by 09:25, throughput recovered ~70% of baseline. Still not back to baseline; P95 remains elevated.

I’m attaching a short kv snapshot we pulled from Cartwave (they shared it) and my runtime log extract (cartwave_5xx_sample.log).

Next steps: full heaptrace & kernel logs from GPU hosts + replicate with internal stress harness.

-Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Olivia / Cartwave SREs,

Thanks for partnering with us on the war-room this morning. Below is a concise summary, actions taken, and next steps. We’ll follow up with a formal RCA and remediation plan within 48 hours.

Summary (what happened):
- At ~08:28 PT we observed autoscaler instability on the yolk-13b-quantized pool that triggered repeated scale-up/scale-down cycles. Those cycles exposed a transient kernel OOM/retry path which amplified request queuing and precipitated higher 5xx rates and increased P95 latency.

Immediate mitigating actions (what we did):
- Pinned affected traffic to the stable quantized runtime variant (09:10 PT) to avoid the retry path.
- Paused aggressive scale-down to stop instance churn (09:12 PT).
- Temporary throttling policy applied to lower-priority background workloads to free capacity (09:18 PT).

Impact & customer commitments:
- Customer-visible error rate peaked ~4.3%; after mitigations we reduced to ~0.9% and recovered ~85% of baseline throughput by 10:15 PT.
- We will deliver an RCA with timeline and a proposed remediation within 48 hours.
- As a gesture of goodwill pending RCA, Redwood’s leadership has approved a credit offer up to two months of committed capacity; Legal and Finance will finalize terms.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Karthik: gather GPU host kernel logs, autoscaler debug dump, and reproduce with stress harness (ETA 24 hrs).
- Marissa: coordinate customer comms and draft credit language with Legal/Finance (ETA 6 hrs).
- David: confirm credit terms and finance approval path.
- Laura: executive-facing brief for the Cartwave executive team and Redwood CEO (ETA 8 hrs).

Attachments: cartwave_5xx_sample.log, cartwave_kv_snapshot.json, cartwave_sla_request.pdf
